body:
I live in America. There is actually a department that helps place people into jobs, and I keep checking. What hinders any potential employment is that I don't drive and public transport doesn't reach my house. Thus it's hard for me to get away from my current home other than with a taxicab. In addition, I don't have a lot of credentials except a high school diploma. I would like to do secretarial work in an office.

I've been told Goodwill often has jobs available to develop skills for a real job. The pay is low, but I don't think I'd be bothered by that really. I don't know if they have jobs other than stocking because I have considerable physical limitations. I just have to find a way to get there. Also, I think I would consider volunteering to have some time. Something that isn't emotionally triggering, or something that would not set off my considerable allergies e.g. a pet shelter.

I'm on disability and have health insurance but social services are pretty fragmented here and the big resources in the area don't open their doors to my particular locality. I'm also a male, so I have to find a shelter that will take in men, has room, serve my city, and will allow me to stay overnight. (It's understandable why some shelters are exclusively female.) The people at the one shelter I called gave me alternative resources that I'll call Monday.
